purpose: replace 'a local build of unrecorded provenance' with a reproducible-build verdict wherever the source can be named, and measure how far short of byte-identity the toolchain falls

measuredFact.claim: byte-identical rebuild is not a reachable acceptance bar, because the builder is not bit-reproducible for a fixed source and output name
measuredFact.evidence: bash: 1,403,134 of 1,403,135 bytes identical to a CLI 0.26.9 rebuild of tree-sitter-bash@0.25.1; the single differing byte is in the wasm DATA section (a segment descriptor), i.e. a linker/emcc configuration difference rather than a grammar difference
measuredFact.consequence: M63 #953 must accept measured behaviour over identity; this turns that position into a measurement

policy.nearMissIsNeverAMatch: an 'equivalent' grade requires an identical prefix AND <=64 differing bytes AND a named section; anything else is 'different'
policy.neverWritesToWasm: builds happen in a temp dir and are only compared. Bytes in wasm/ change only through F11, by hand, with a review document.
policy.outputNameMatters: the rebuild is given the SHIPPED build-output name, because that name is written into the module's name section; using a convenient filename manufactures a difference that has nothing to do with the grammar
